what: The CB doc (pointed to for "any CB-related issue") documents push/pop COUNT balance but never the CB WRAP invariant: a CB page count must be an exact multiple of EVERY push/pop quantum used on that core, because neither endpoint may wrap mid-transfer. Producer: llk_push_tiles LLK_ASSERT(remaining >= num_words, "CB push_back: fifo_wr_ptr would exceed fifo_limit") (tt_metal/hw/ckernels/*/metal/llk_io/llk_io_pack.h). Consumer: cb_pop_front ASSERT(fifo_rd_ptr <= fifo_limit), wrapping only on exact equality, under the comment "consumer always reads from contiguous memory, it cannot wrap" (tt_metal/hw/inc/api/dataflow/dataflow_api.h:267-272). Grep for wrap|contiguous|fifo_limit|multiple of in the doc returns nothing relevant. This is not a corner case: it bit the binding op_design.md in TWO independent places at once -- (a) cb_output_tiles capacity (wrpb+1)*W against a wrpb*W-page pop quantum, which for wrpb=8,W=1 gives a 9-page CB popped 8 at a time, so the second batch straddles the limit; and (b) the ragged column tail, whose two per-core quanta (block_width_tiles and block_width_tail_tiles) cannot both divide one capacity without lcm-sizing. Both are reachable on ordinary geometries in this op INPUTS set. Cost was recovered only by reading three LLK/dataflow sources to derive the rule, then re-deriving the block-extent selection (divisor-of-C) and CB depth (batch multiples) around it. Failure mode is nasty: an LLK_ASSERT visible only under --dev, or silent corruption in production mode, on a kernel whose push/pop COUNTS balance perfectly -- i.e. it passes every check the doc actually teaches.
suggest: Add a "CB wrap / transfer quantum" section to ttnn-cb-memory-fundamentals.md next to the sync-count invariant, stating: (1) the invariant (num_pages % quantum == 0 for every quantum on that core, and all quanta on a core must be commensurate); (2) the two assert citations above as the enforcement; (3) that COUNT balance does NOT imply wrap safety, so this is a second independent audit; (4) the two safe patterns -- size the capacity as an integer number of BATCHES rather than batch+1, and keep one quantum per core (for a ragged tail, either make the extent divide the axis or size to the lcm); (5) the escape hatch for a genuinely variable batch, i.e. cap the batch at ((fifo_limit - fifo_rd_ptr) / fifo_page_size) read off get_local_cb_interface. Also worth a forward-pointer from blocking-model.md:184, which says "any linear block access must be contiguous or explicitly wrap-safe" but gives no rule for how -- that line is exactly where a planner needs the CB doc link, since the planner cannot be expected to derive an LLK assert.
